tagline: A modular fusion protein that uses the eye's own sugar coating as an anchor, delivered in a hydrogel, so dry eye medicine stays put.
summary: Dry eye disease affects an estimated 34.6% of people globally and 21.3% of Canadian adults, and the central problem is not the drug but the delivery: blinking and tear drainage clear a topical therapeutic within minutes. gleyeco treats the ocular glycocalyx as a docking site rather than a barrier, fusing a Galectin-3 carbohydrate-recognition domain (binding Core 1 O-glycans on mucins), a tandem pair of the 12-residue hyaluronic-acid-binding peptide HABpep, and IL-1RA (anakinra) as the therapeutic payload, delivered from a crosslinked PEG/hyaluronic acid hydrogel as a drop or a contact lens. The team built a five-stage dry lab pipeline with its own acronyms - GLARE, InSiGHT, VOIR, I-SPY, HOPE - that chooses the target, engineers the binder, sets the valency, predicts the yield and tunes the gel, and released GLARE as an installable Python package. It won Best Entrepreneurship on an unusually rigorous commercial case (38-patient survey, two clinician letters of support, a letter of intent from a clinic, competitor matrix against Restasis/Cequa/Xiidra, PESTEL, 10-year plan) and was nominated for the Inclusivity Award for an open-access Inclusivity in Research course, an Adaptive Technology Kit and a rural teachers' programme.
awards: Canadian iGEM GCI Conference: Best Human Practices and Entrepreneurship; Best Overall Poster Runner-Up

dry.frameworks: Five named operations, each handing its result to the next. GLARE (Glycan-Lectin Analysis for Recognition and Evaluation) mines global glycan databases of 50,000+ catalogued sequences, filters to the 134 unique structures documented in ocular tissue (cornea, tear film, lacrimal gland), confirms O-glycans dominate, then screens Galectin-3's off-target risk across other organs and three cancers under identical statistics with multiple-hypothesis-testing correction, and finally re-runs the analysis under a dry-eye disease signature, finding the disease phenotype exposes over 2.5x more accessible binding sites. InSiGHT (In Silico Glycan Honed Targeting) engineers Galectin-3 to favour Core 1 over LacNAc: mutation sites were chosen from the literature (H46, N48, R50, N62, W69, E72 hydrogen-bonding residues plus nearby polar R32, E53, R74), a Clustal Omega multiple sequence alignment of all available mammalian galectins from PDB and NCBI (which excluded the perfectly conserved W69 and flagged the poorly conserved E53), and a PyMOL structural alignment of 12 galectin CRDs against Galectin-3 (PDB 3ZSJ, 0.86 Angstrom) that identified the E53-V58 loop and the I33/N31 positions as differentiators; a Python script generates mutant combinations, FoldX builds the structures, HADDOCK and Schrodinger dock Core 1 and LacNAc in parallel after AutoDock Vina proved unable to handle large flexible glycans, and GROMACS scores binding strength - batched across RunPod for parallel FoldX jobs. Ten mutants (Alpha through Kappa) went to the bench. VOIR (Valency Optimization and Integrated Retention) uses the valentBind model to compute bivalent avidity as a function of linker length and glycan target density, concluding that a second binding domain gives the largest gain, a third a moderate one, and a fourth nothing - and recommending (GGGGS)6-16 linkers. I-SPY (I Shall Produce Yield) curates the BL21(DE3)-based iBB1018 genome-scale reconstruction in COBRApy for the SHuffle T7 Express chassis, adds a demand reaction for the heterologous fusion protein, and runs flux balance analysis to locate metabolic bottlenecks. HOPE (Hydrogel Optimization for Pharmacokinetic Evaluation) models mesh size with the Peppas-Merrill and then the Canal-Peppas form of Flory-Rehner, using interpolated PEGDA swelling data and MeHA degree of methacrylation, and derives protein diffusivity from it.
dry.dataviz: The modelling page is organised as a relay: five labelled operations (Choose, Improve, Multiply, Produce, Deliver) in a flow a reader clicks into, each with its own write-up and its own Impressiveness/Design/Validation/Exemplarity framing. The software page embeds a live in-browser CLI simulator for GLARE with clickable example commands (--cell eye, --binding-galectins eye, --target-compare eye core1 stn, --disease-compare dry_eye) so a judge can run the pipeline's logic without installing Python. For audiences without a biology background the team built the gleyecobuddies: Lecto (Galectin-3, with the binding site built into the character design), Ana (IL-1RA, a red plus sign) and Happy (HABpep, a blue rectangle standing for a wall that holds the drug in place), deliberately layered on top of the standard Symbol Nomenclature for Glycans rather than replacing it, and justified as serving visual learners, neurodivergent people and children. All InSiGHT results are reported with the predictors' disagreements visible rather than averaged.
dry.datascience: The team repeatedly uses modelling to avoid spending bench time, and reports the limits of each prediction. GLARE's stated limitations are unusually frank: the database records which structures have been documented in a tissue, not how much is displayed, so enrichment results describe structural patterns and must not be read as surface density; the diseased-versus-healthy split is built from literature signatures rather than a labelled patient dataset, and the pipeline is written so a real patient-derived list can be dropped in unchanged; binding strengths come from published microarray data, not from their own fusion protein; the tissue panel is small, and the cervix moved along the same mucin O-glycan axis as the eye so other mucosal surfaces would need direct testing. In InSiGHT they caught their own pipeline's instability - mutating key polar residues to alanine did not abolish predicted binding as it should, and one HADDOCK run gave mutant Gamma -6.495 kcal/mol against Core 1 while a separate run of the same mutant gave -3.84, which they report as evidence the pipeline needs repeated runs. For VOIR they state the point is the optimal linker length range, not the headline avidity ratio, because the values are literature-derived estimates not validated in vitro. For HOPE the model behaved as theory predicts (mesh falling from 16 nm at 5% w/v PEGDA to about 10 nm at 25%, predicted protein diffusivity from about 60 to 37 micrometres squared per second against 97 in free water) and they say plainly they could not build the equivalent alginate model, and that an OpenFOAM CFD attempt failed because the corneal absorption boundary condition had to be written in C++ and did not run reliably, so they fell back to a 1D Python model for sensitivity analysis.
dry.software: GLARE, released as an importable Python package (v0.2.0, Python 3.10+) at https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/software/ualberta/software-glare, runnable from the command line with a clear module structure separating tissue validation, binding analysis, cross-tissue comparison, disease signatures and docking-structure generation behind a single pipeline interface, with generalised inputs so another team can point it at a different tissue, lectin or glycan. A browser-based CLI simulator on the wiki lets anyone try it without installing. The Adaptive Technology Kit is an open-source hardware release: 3D-printable PCR strip-tube and microfuge-tube openers (in multiple design variants, because user testing showed different researchers preferred different models), an agarose gel loader, an SDS gel loader, a braille stamper, a keyboard tool, a pencil holder, a non-slip tray, a microscope phone holder, and a tactile map of the iGEM lab with published blueprints. A Synthetic Biology Lab Manual and the full Rural Teachers Synbiosium materials are published as free PDFs, as is the DNA-as-Code Kit.

good.publicEngagement: Three distinct, durable programmes rather than one-off booths. (1) The Inclusivity in Research Course, an open-access training run through Google Classroom, built from a nationwide survey and expert consultations, with modules on a Native Land activity, the team's own 'Just Ask' framework and neurodivergent inclusion, creating open spaces, blind and visually impaired inclusion, Deaf and hard-of-hearing inclusion, racialized people, women and 2SLGBTQIA+ and gender minorities, navigating reporting processes, and an accessibility resource bank - each with downloadable slides, infographics and interactive summaries. It was piloted with their own team, neighbouring labs and Canadian iGEM teams, and the three pieces of pilot feedback (offer multiple learning formats, add scenario-based practice, cover more groups) were each implemented as narrated audio and slideshows, self-reflection prompts and real lab case studies, and two new modules. (2) The Rural Teachers Synbiosium, a half-day online professional development event for rural Alberta teachers, mapped explicitly onto the Alberta middle and high school curriculum, covering case studies and how to secure funding, with three guest speakers including Amino Labs CEO Julie Legault, 9 free hands-on kits distributed (teachers chose between a one-day yeast-fermentation race car and a multi-day pigment-engineering agar art project) and all materials shipped in advance to lower the burden. (3) Public outreach at K-Days, an Edmonton summer festival, where visitors attempted lab tasks while simulating different visual impairments, plus a DNA-as-code bracelet activity, and tabling at Alberta's Women in STEM week after being invited by the Alberta Women in Science Network. The team also presented at the Canadian Glycomics Symposium, CNAS Research Day, Darwin Day, Cell Biology Research Day, the RE Peter Conference and the Canadian iGEM GCI Conference, and ran a hands-on workshop at Canmore Collegiate High School - which is what revealed the rural access problem and started the Synbiosium.
good.ihp: Every stakeholder entry is logged as a Key Insight paired with an Action Taken, and the actions are real design reversals. Dr Warren Wakarchuk (Scientific Director of GlycoNet) warned that small-molecule binding pockets hold cargo too tightly to release on the eye and that yeast adds problematic sugar tags, and noted eukaryotic tissue autofluoresces green under UV - so the team abandoned the binding-pocket release concept, chose E. coli over yeast, switched the reporter from GFP to mScarlet, and retargeted abundant normal ocular glycans instead of rare disease-specific ones. Dr Lisa Willis (glyco-immunology) raised immune safety and challenged them to test whether the Galectin-3 and HA domains cooperate or compete for binding - so instead of assuming more binding is better, they redesigned the experimental plan to measure each domain separately by isothermal titration calorimetry. Dr Carr advised narrowing from retinal delivery to corneal inflammation in dry eye with IL-1RA cargo and offered Xenopus eye tissue for ex vivo testing. An advisor recommended the SHuffle T7 strain and told them their fusion protein was not complex enough to justify a chaperone plasmid, so they dropped it. Dr Amandeep helped unify the five separate models into one pipeline and suggested using eye images as GLARE input to make it diagnostic - the team pursued it, found it infeasible, said so, and redirected to modelling; he also pointed them to RunPod, which is why FoldX now runs in parallel. Jezlyn warned that chemical and UV crosslinking would denature mScarlet, so they moved to physical ionic crosslinking with calcium chloride, wrote autoclaving protocols for sterility, and were pointed at the Peppas-Merrill and Flory-Rehner equations that became HOPE. Dr Cortez told them not to add a second nickel column but to optimise their existing HisTrap/FPLC wash stringency, which they did and documented on Coomassie gels. Optometrist Dr Abdo Kattan explained that his multi-product dry eye package (omega 3s, drops, lid wipes, goggles) has very low compliance because it is time-consuming, expensive and impossible to attribute benefit to - which refocused the whole project on one affordable single-product treatment. Separately, CD44 was dropped entirely as the HA-retention domain in favour of tandem HABpep after it kept appearing in the insoluble fraction and the literature revealed isoforms linked to cancer therapy resistance. On the inclusivity side, Nicholas Piroddi (a medical researcher with autism) was consulted, then consulted a second time to review how the course represented neurodiversity, which added the institutional reporting-pathways module; ASVI's input became the blind and visually impaired module; and user testing of the 3D-printed tube openers at the WinSTEM expo is why the kit ships multiple variants of the same tool.
good.realWorld: The strongest undergraduate commercial case of the five. Evidence of demand is tabulated by customer role with the strength of evidence named: letters of support from Dr Abdo Kattan and Dr Matthew Benson (and a signed letter of intent from Kattan's clinic to work with them), 86% of 38 surveyed dry eye patients interested in a synthetic biology treatment, and an application in interview stage with the Nucleate Canada accelerator. The patient survey plus three clinician interviews produced five explicit unmet needs - fewer doses, longer retention, no burning or stinging, targeted anti-inflammatory action, contact lens compatibility - which the product is then measured against. A competitor matrix compares gleyeco line by line with Restasis (AbbVie), Cequa (Sun Pharma) and Xiidra (Bausch + Lomb) on mechanism, dosing, time to effect, clinical evidence, tolerability, lens compatibility, 30-day cost and Canadian availability, citing prescribing information and Drugs.com prices as of 15 October 2026, and crucially labels gleyeco's own entries as design goals that preclinical and clinical data must confirm. The gap identified is precise: every anti-inflammatory option is dosed at least twice daily and none occupies targeted once-daily treatment. TAM/SAM/SOM, regional opportunity, bottom-up dynamics, current distribution network, a Size-Potential-Access analysis, a beachhead market defined by role (users, decision makers, payers, pharmaceutical partners), a 10-year implementation plan and an exit strategy all follow. The PESTEL analysis is specific to Canadian biotech: Health Canada's Reliance Order syncing review with the FDA if filed within 120 days, Alberta Innovates and FAST cutting trial start-up from 90+ to 45 days, PMPRB price controls pushing them toward private payers first, over 75% of Canadian life-science investment coming from abroad so Phase 2 needs a partner, the USD/CAD rate at 1.4, and the fact that the RE Peter Conference and Jamboree disclosures start the novelty clock (12 months in Canada, absolute novelty required in Europe). Clinical milestones were set directly from a clinician's roadmap, and lab eye models have been offered by two separate researchers for the move from proof of concept to preclinical.

gemsTakeaway: Copy UAlberta's two-column human practices habit - every conversation written as one Key Insight and one Action Taken, where the action is a concrete reversal (GFP to mScarlet, yeast to E. coli, CD44 dropped for HABpep, chemical crosslinking dropped for calcium) - because it forces a team to admit when advice changed nothing. The other directly adaptable asset is their rural pivot: they went in planning to help schools found competition teams, learned from the teachers that capacity was the real constraint, and instead built a curriculum-aligned half-day online session with pre-shipped kits and a free lab manual, which is exactly the model a Taiwanese research centre could run for under-resourced schools.
